title: Review hardware RT flashlight request changes
objective: Review Builder's hardware ray tracing changes for examples/flashlight live realistic mode, focusing on correctness, regressions, Unreal/CVar/property probing risks, and test adequacy before the user reruns the simulator.
instructions: Read the Builder result and inspect the diffs for examples/flashlight/run.py, examples/flashlight/flashlight_profiles.py, and tests/test_orbit_collection_validation.py.
Review whether realistic mode requests hardware RT by default while non-realistic behavior remains unchanged.
Review the chosen hardware RT/Lumen CVars for obvious mistakes or unsupported assumptions, using local project/engine config context where possible.
Review the runtime console variable readback logic and the spotlight ray-traced shadow method/property probing for false positives, bad argument types, or possible crashes.
Review tests for meaningful coverage and any brittle assumptions.

artifacts: Realistic live flashlight mode now requests hardware ray tracing by default via launch INI and runtime console commands, with --disable-hardware-ray-tracing as an opt-out.
Flashlight live mode now logs hardware RT requested settings separately from runtime command/readback state and attempts ray-traced spotlight shadow intent when hardware RT is requested.

expected_outputs: ResultPacket with findings ordered by severity, approval/blocker status, and any exact remediation recommendations.
definition_of_done: Tower can tell the user whether the RT changes are safe enough for manual runtime testing or need Builder fixes first.
